# secopsctl skill

Print the agent operating guide embedded in the binary (offline)

## skill

Print the agent operating guide embedded in the binary (offline)

```text
secopsctl skill
```

```text
Emit the secopsctl agent operating guide baked into the binary: the
two-auth-plane model, the mutation ritual, the config-as-code loop, the
self-discovery commands, and the gotchas the per-command --help can't express.

Self-contained — `go install danny.vn/secops/cmd/secopsctl@latest` ships only
the binary, so this is how an agent retrieves the guide without the repo:
  secopsctl skill            print the guide (--json wraps {name,description,body})
  secopsctl skill install    write it into an agent skills dir for auto-detection

Detect-then-install: an agent reads `secopsctl skill --json` to discover the
skill, then (once the user approves) runs `secopsctl skill install`.
```

## skill install

Install the operating guide into an agent skills directory

```text
secopsctl skill install [flags]
```

```text
Write the embedded guide to <skills-dir>/secopsctl/SKILL.md so an agent
harness detects it as a first-class skill. The default skills directory is
$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills (or ~/.claude/skills); --dir overrides it (e.g.
--dir ./.claude/skills to install into the current project). Writing a local
file only — no network, no live instance. Idempotent: a no-op when the file
already matches; if it exists with different content it is left untouched
unless --force (so a hand-tuned copy is never clobbered silently).
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dir` | string | - | skills directory to install into (default $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills or ~/.claude/skills) |
| `--force` | bool | false | overwrite an existing SKILL.md whose content differs |
